t: Section 221(d)(2) of the National Housing Act is amended by striking out “a displaced family” at the end of the first proviso and inserting in lieu thereof “the mortgagor”.

fable.w: This is a purely technical amendment substituting one phrase for another in the National Housing Act. It involves no consultation, hearing, rulemaking, advisory body, or right to sue, and no party outside the federal government is brought into any federal decision. There is no real tempting contrary reading, since "displaced family" and "mortgagor" are merely terms describing mortgage insurance eligibility rather than participants in a decision.
fable.s: Section 221(d)(2) of the National Housing Act is amended by striking out “a displaced family” at the end of the first proviso and inserting in lieu thereof “the mortgagor”.

qwen_block.w: This section is a technical amendment to the National Housing Act, changing the definition of a party involved in a housing transaction from 'a displaced family' to 'the mortgagor'. It does not establish any process for public comment, consultation with outside entities, or advisory boards. It merely alters the statutory text regarding who is eligible or involved in a specific housing provision, which is an administrative or definitional change, not a participation mechanism.
qwen_block.s: Section 221(d)(2) of the National Housing Act is amended by striking out “a displaced family” at the end of the first proviso and inserting in lieu thereof “the mortgagor”.

opus.w: This section only replaces one term with another in the National Housing Act. It sets up no process for outside parties to consult on or shape a federal decision. Mentioning private parties such as a mortgagor does not count as participation, because the text gives them no role in any federal decision.
opus.s: Section 221(d)(2) of the National Housing Act is amended by striking out “a displaced family” at the end of the first proviso and inserting in lieu thereof “the mortgagor”.
opus.b: **Step 1, the tempting reading:** The amendment names outside private parties ("a displaced family," "the mortgagor"). That might suggest someone outside the government is involved. It fails against the definition. The section only swaps one word in an existing housing statute. It creates no comment period, hearing, advisory body, consultation, rulemaking authority or right to sue.

qwen_chat.w: This section is a simple textual amendment to the National Housing Act, changing the reference from 'a displaced family' to 'the mortgagor'. It does not establish any process for outside parties to consult with the government, serve on an advisory board, attend a public hearing, or otherwise participate in a federal decision. It merely defines the subject of a provision.
qwen_chat.s: Section 221(d)(2) of the National Housing Act is amended by striking out “a displaced family” at the end of the first proviso and inserting in lieu thereof “the mortgagor”.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that changing the beneficiary of a housing provision ("displaced family" to "mortgagor") implies a change in who participates in the program. However, this is merely a textual amendment defining the recipient of a benefit or the subject of a rule, not a procedural requirement for outside parties to consult with the government or participate in a decision-making process. The definition of participation requires consultation, coordination, advisory boards with non-federal members, public hearings, or rights to sue. This section contains none of those elements.
